name: comparison-matrix
title: Comparison Matrix
description: A compact multi-criterion matrix for comparing two options without replacing the before-and-after component.
author: iPolloWork

ai.instructions: Separate option names with |. Format each row as Criterion|Left value|Right value and separate rows with semicolons.

variables.label: Semantic cue times
variables.description: JSON event IDs to measured scene-relative seconds. Empty uses authored timings; this is not word alignment.

events.action: Reveal and focus the next semantic item
Reveal and focus the next semantic item
Reveal and focus the next semantic item
Reveal and focus the next semantic item

useWhen: Compare exactly two options using 1–4 common criteria.
avoidWhen: Do not compare more than two options, incompatible units or omit unfavorable evidence to force a winner.

inputRules.title: Supply real title within the declared character limit. Do not substitute demo text.
inputRules.options: Exactly two nonempty option names separated by |; apply the same criterion and unit to both.
inputRules.rows: Supply 1–4 entries separated by ";", each with exactly 3 nonempty fields separated by "|". Keep each field within 64 characters.
inputRules.winner: Choose only a declared option; do not force a winner without evidence.

readingOrder: Compare one common criterion at a time

cueBindings.step-1: When narration reaches rows 1, reveal and focus the next semantic item. Do not infer a word timestamp from character count.
cueBindings.step-2: When narration reaches rows 2, reveal and focus the next semantic item. Do not infer a word timestamp from character count.
cueBindings.step-3: When narration reaches rows 3, reveal and focus the next semantic item. Do not infer a word timestamp from character count.
cueBindings.step-4: When narration reaches rows 4, reveal and focus the next semantic item. Do not infer a word timestamp from character count.
cueBindings.resolve: At the concluding narration clause, settle the shown evidence; allow the authored final reading hold.

fallback.overflow: Split at a real semantic boundary or use a more suitable component; never truncate items or shrink text until unreadable.
fallback.missingInput: Resolve the actual required input or report the missing content; do not substitute demo defaults or custom graphics under recipes-only policy.
fallback.timingMismatch: Bind measured cueTimes once, preserving order, authored action durations and a 0.7–4s final hold. Split at a narration boundary when the sequence cannot fit; do not stretch speech or create a frozen tail.
fallback.inapplicable: Choose another validated recipe whose narrative job fits, split at a meaningful boundary, or report the library gap. Under recipes-only policy, never author custom graphics or force-fit content.

acceptance: Every active declared event changes its actual visible target; forward and backward seeking restore the same state.
The final state remains readable without cropped or overlapping important text, with honest source and timing metadata.
Identify both options → Compare one common criterion at a time → Read the full matrix. Preserve this reading order and the source qualifiers.
Test Chinese content, the minimum and maximum supported item counts, and one rejected overflow or malformed input.
